items.headline: Financial Advisors and Retirees' Risk-taking -- by Allison T. Cole, Maarten Meeuwis, Alessandro Previtero, Noah Stoffman
items.summary: Advised retirees keep about two-thirds of their portfolios in equities well into old age—30 to 40 percentage points more than non-advised retirees, target-date funds, or common rules of thumb. These allocations reflect active choices rather than inertia, and they adjust gradually toward a new advisor’s investment style following advisor switches. Equity shares rise with relationship tenure, and advisor influence is strongest among clients with low financial knowledge or risk tolerance, consistent with trust facilitating risk-taking.

items.headline: Doing Better at Doing Good: Lessons from a Bayesian Meta-Analysis After 20 Years of Poverty Graduation Programs -- by Samantha Carter, Edward Jee, Dean Karlan, Patrick Premand
items.summary: Multifaceted poverty Graduation programs that aim to increase income generating activities for low-income households are being rapidly adopted and scaled by nonprofit organizations and governments. This paper conducts a Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis of 49 studies (encompassing 81 treatment variations) on poverty Graduation programs, defined as containing at least three of five components: consumption support, savings facilitation, skills training, coaching, and a lumpsum transfer. The analysis finds large gains across economic and psychosocial outcomes: monthly consumption rises by 38 USD PPP (11 percent), income by 28 USD PPP (15 percent), alongside improvements in savings, assets, food security, mental health, and women’s empowerment.

detail.method_architecture: This paper conducts a Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis of 49 studies (encompassing 81 treatment variations) on poverty Graduation programs, defined as containing at least three of five components: consumption support, savings facilitation, skills training, coaching, and a lumpsum transfer. The analysis finds large gains across economic and psychosocial outcomes: monthly consumption rises by 38 USD PPP (11 percent), income by 28 USD PPP (15 percent), alongside improvements in savings, assets, food security, mental health, and women’s empowerment.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: Beyond these average treatment effects, three results stand out. First, programs with large transfers (at least 400 USD PPP) have larger treatment effects but are not more cost-effective. Second, more expensive programs generate larger treatment effects, but the improvements are not commensurate with the cost increases; thus, lower cost programs tend to be more cost-effective. Third, programs implemented from 2016 onward perform considerably better than those implemented prior to 2016: benefit-cost ratios from 2016 onward are 5.39, compared to 2.89 through 2015. Neither changes in cost nor in high-level design (components) explain this upward trend. Considering other heavily studied interventions, the results show a similar upward trend for treatment effects on behavior change from financial education but not for unconditional cash transfers. The paper hypothesizes a mechanism of continuous sector-community learning and improved implementation quality.

items.headline: Policy Deterrence: Strategic Investment in U.S. Broadband -- by Karam Kang, Mo Xiao
items.summary: Can firms influence policy through investment? Using 2010--2019 U.S. broadband deployment and state policy data, we find that large internet service providers expand capacity more in electorally competitive counties. Greater large-provider capacity in swing counties is associated with fewer subsequent entry- and investment-facilitating policies, especially rights-of-way accommodations that reduce deployment barriers faced by smaller providers.

detail.abstract_excerpt: Can firms influence policy through investment? Using 2010--2019 U.S. broadband deployment and state policy data, we find that large internet service providers expand capacity more in electorally competitive counties. Greater large-provider capacity in swing counties is associated with fewer subsequent entry- and investment-facilitating policies, especially rights-of-way accommodations that reduce deployment barriers faced by smaller providers. To interpret these patterns, we develop a model in which a large firm's capacity can reduce the policymaker's gain from intervention. In the model, policy deterrence raises the large firm's market share and can reduce total deployment.

items.headline: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
items.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03519-6 Resonances in ultracold collisions couple to scattering states, causing interactions and loss. Now it is shown that the interference of Feshbach resonances creates a bound state in the continuum that decouples from elastic and inelastic scattering.

items.headline: Active-flow-driven DNA remodelling generates millimetre-scale mechanical oscillations
items.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03505-y Active matter can exhibit turbulent or coherent flows. Now it is shown that active flows can entangle DNA polymers, leading to a non-equilibrium transition from disordered turbulence to periodic motion.

items.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03520-z Phase-space conservation bars coherence enhancement in passive linear optics, a limit often bypassed by gain or feedback. Here conservative nonlinearity reshapes phase space, thermodynamically driving incoherent light towards a coherent equilibrium.

detail.problem_context: Summary Project Zero compared two automated tools used by Google to find vulnerabilities in Chrome’s JavaScript engine, V8, on a regular basis.
detail.method_architecture: Fuzzilli is a generative JavaScript engine fuzzer and BigSleep is an LLM-based bug finding system. In the past six months, BigSleep found more vulnerabilities than Fuzzilli (45 versus 37) with a 25% overlap in the specific bugs reported.
detail.findings_tradeoffs: Since this comparison methodology has a tendency to underestimate overlap, we also performed dedicated experiments to test theoretical overlap in vulnerabilities reported since 2023. These experiments estimated overlap at roughly 60%. Regardless of which value is accurate, a substantial portion of vulnerabilities were discoverable by only LLMs or only fuzzing. While it is extremely promising that LLMs have become able to find so many vulnerabilities so quickly, fuzzing and LLMs are still complementary approaches. We recommend vendors perform both fuzzing and agentic analysis of their code to maximize the number of vulnerabilities that get reported before they impact users.

detail.abstract_excerpt: Summary Project Zero compared two automated tools used by Google to find vulnerabilities in Chrome’s JavaScript engine, V8, on a regular basis. Fuzzilli is a generative JavaScript engine fuzzer and BigSleep is an LLM-based bug finding system. In the past six months, BigSleep found more vulnerabilities than Fuzzilli (45 versus 37) with a 25% overlap in the specific bugs reported. Since this comparison methodology has a tendency to underestimate overlap, we also performed dedicated experiments to test theoretical overlap in vulnerabilities reported since 2023. These experiments estimated overlap at roughly 60%. Regardless of which value is accurate, a substantial portion of vulnerabilities were discoverable by only LLMs or only fuzzing. While it is extremely promising that LLMs have become able to find so many vulnerabilities so quickly, fuzzing and LLMs are still complementary approaches. We recommend vendors perform both fuzzing and agentic analysis of their code to maximize the number of vulnerabilities that get reported before they impact users.

items.headline: How to fix a bug in a fix
items.summary: Project Zero often works with software vendors to remediate the vulnerabilities we report and provide broader guidance on making software more secure. Some vendors express concern about potential scenarios in which they are unable to fix vulnerabilities that are causing immediate user harm, due to limitations in their patch delivery systems. Since Project Zero encounters a wide array of systems designed to protect users in the case of exceptional exploitation scenarios, both through vendor discussions and security reviews, we want to share what we’ve learned.

items.headline: Yapay zekânın yönünü sadece piyasanın belirlemesine izin vermeyin
items.summary: Bilim Akademisi üyesi, 2024 Nobel İktisat Ödülü sahibi Daron Acemoğlu’nun 27 Haziran 2026 Koç Üniversitesi Mezuniyet töreninde yaptığı konuşmanın metni Acemoğlu’nun katkısıyla yayıma hazırlanmıştır.[1]Mezuniyet Töreni Konuşması 2026, Prof. Dr. Daron Acemoğlu, 27 Haziran 2026, Koç Üniversitesi YouTube Dünyanın en seçkin üniversitelerinden birinden mezun olduğunuz için sizleri tebrik ederim. Bunun gururunu duymanızı hepimiz gerçekten çok istiyoruz.

items.summary: Sinan Alper’le yaptığımız Meraklısına Bilim sohbetinde Akademim Yayınlarından 2026 yazında yayımlanmış “Yanlış Bilgi Üzerine” başlıklı kitabı üzerinden yanlış bilgi türlerini, insanların yanlış bilgiyi neden yaydıklarını, gerçek-ötesi (post-truth) kavramını, toplumsal kutuplaşma ve bilime güvenle ilişkisini konuştuk. Moderatör: Defne Üçer Şaylan Sinan Alper, yüksek lisansını London School of Economics and Political Science’ta, doktorasını ODTÜ’de tamamlamıştır. items.headline: Güneş gençliğinde Dünya’nın birkaç katı kütlede bir gezegeni “yutmuş” olabilir
